text:
Peyton Krebs plays a passer's game. He has 11 points in 22 games, ten of them assists, and only 15 shots, which is very few for a forward playing 14.6 minutes a night. Buffalo has given him more lately (16.1 minutes over his last ten), and in an Audacy interview he talked about his chemistry with Tage Thompson.

The Buffalo News noted he is approaching an NHL milestone, and the Sabres posted a sit-down with Rob Ray titled "Work Ethic Will Beat Anything Else," which fits a player whose value shows up in hits (44) and puck movement more than goals.

The numbers ask a fair question about how sustainable the assists are. The Sabres have scored 6.23 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and five-on-five they are roughly even with him (50% of expected goals, the quality of chances). Evolving-Hockey valued him at 1.5 wins last season but flagged that his results ran well ahead of his chances (0.3 expected wins). His one goal on 2.93 expected is the other side of the luck ledger. We'd watch whether he starts shooting more as the minutes grow.
